reason: Not refuted. All opcodes are real on the 65SC12 (BRA, BCS, SBC imm, STA abs,X; no BBR/BBS/RMB/SMB). Carry: on the first entry C=1 because sky_H is always 23, 26 or 28 (sky_heights, or sky_h,X copied from it) and sky_t=L+1<=8, so SBC sky_t does not borrow; LDX and BRA leave C alone. On re-entry via BCS taken C=1, and SBC #8 with A>=9 keeps C=1, so SBC #&80 sees C=1 every time, as with the old SEC. Fall-out of BCS (A<9, C=0) reaches .top with the same A, X and C as the old BCC top. Stores are the same and in the same order. .more is used only here. Cycles (sky_rl/rh/rt/rb/rn are absolute at &BC90-&BCAD, X small, so no indexed page crossing in either version): new layout DE7B LDX, DE7D BRA ->DE8A, skyg_d_next DE7F, body DE8A-DEA9, BCS at DEAA ->DE7F, all within page DE, so there are no branch page penalties (none in the old either). Per execution with k iterations: SEC -2k, non-last iterations BCS taken 3 vs BCC not taken 2 + BRA 3 (-2 each), last iteration BCS not taken 2 vs BCC taken 3 (-1), entry BRA +3: saving 4k-4. H in {23,26,28} and L in 0..7 give k=2..4, so 4 to 12 cycles. The claimed 9.8 is k of about 3.45 on average, which fits H mostly 26/28. Bytes: SEC -1, one BRA swapped for another, BCC swapped for BCS: -1. Everything after the window moves down 1 byte: .top DEAC, split loop DEC1-DF1C. BNE whole, BCC whole and BNE split cross DE/DF before and after, so their costs are unchanged. sky_col_row and sky_col_check stay wholly in DF (DF1E-DF63), and hazel_b_end is DF64, still below the &E000 ASSERT. No self-modified operands and no data read as code in the region.
